thesisQuality.note: Strong contracted hyperscaler demand, Horizon 1 acceptance and integrated power-to-compute footprint support a strong band; capital intensity and unproven full contract conversion cap the value below exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Rapid AI-cloud expansion and liquidity are offset by FY2026 net loss, large commitments, debt and financing dependence, supporting mixed/unproven rather than strong operating economics.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Independent market evidence shows a high enterprise value relative to trailing revenue; substantial AI optionality exists but present valuation requires meaningful future conversion, placing the factor at the low end of mixed/unproven.

catalystScore.note: Horizon 2-4 commissioning/acceptance and conversion of contracted ARR are multiple material identifiable catalysts, with contractual windows extending into early Q2 2027.

governancePower.note: Formal independent-board and audit/risk oversight requirements plus audited ICFR support an adequate-to-strong governance band, but limited evidence of long-duration capital-allocation outcomes prevents a higher score.

alignment2036.note: Power, data-center and accelerated-compute infrastructure directly serve durable AI/critical digital-infrastructure demand across plausible long-duration scenarios.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Power, data centers, compute and Mirantis software/support create several reusable layers and demand channels, though economics remain dominated by infrastructure deployment.

bottleneckControl.note: Multi-gigawatt site pipeline and integrated power-to-compute capability participate in scarce power/data-center constraints; planned MW are not assumed to be financed, energized or productive.

scenarioRobustness.note: Geographic and vendor diversification plus customer prepayments broaden resilience, while financing, commissioning and customer concentration keep material scenario dependence.

substitutionResilience.note: Integrated infrastructure and qualification/commissioning create friction, but hyperscaler self-build and competing GPU-cloud providers remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Multiple GPU generations and OEM/vendor relationships provide redundancy, but the 10-K explicitly identifies constrained GPU/networking supply and limited supplier sets.

pricingPower.note: Large contract value and tranche prepayments indicate some economic leverage, but comparable unit economics and realized margins are not disclosed, so durable pricing power remains unproven.

risk.note: High capital commitments, $7.976b principal debt, covenant/secured-financing exposure, dilution risk, constrained hardware supply and commissioning/customer concentration create material downside even with strong liquidity and prepayments.

confidence.note: Primary FY2026 SEC filing, issuer governance documents, independent current valuation and same-cycle Scout/Beta source-addressed assists cover all 12 components; remaining unknowns concern future realization rather than missing present evidence.

thesis: IREN can convert scarce power and data-center capacity into an integrated AI-infrastructure platform with contracted hyperscaler demand, but value realization depends on disciplined financing, commissioning and margin conversion.
keyRisk: Capital intensity, leverage, dilution, constrained hardware supply and customer/commissioning concentration can make headline contracted demand materially less valuable than expected.
nextCatalyst: Acceptance and revenue conversion of Microsoft Horizon 2-4 tranches through contractual delivery/grace windows extending into early Q2 2027.
